title: ApprovedPlan
description:
The refactoring plan after the developer's accept/reject pass in the DIWO Plan Approval stage. This is the second critical human-feedback hand-off, and the mirror of FilteredCUQAReport: a step the developer rejected must NEVER reach the SCTVA agent, because a rejected step left in the JSON would be mapped to an SCTVA action and executed.

Produced by backend/domain/plan_normalizer.py::build_approved_plan and returned as `approved_plan` from POST /api/workflows/<id>/plan-decision. It is stored as the workflow's plan_json, which is what POST /api/workflows/<id>/transform defaults to — so the approved-only plan is used even when the caller sends nothing.

It is a RefactoringPlan reduced to the approved steps, plus an `approval` block recording what was rejected. The rejected steps are recorded rather than silently dropped, and the full pre-approval plan is kept separately (plan_full_json) so a rollback from the Transformation stage can offer every step for re-selection.

steps.description: ONLY the steps the developer approved. Steps keep their ORIGINAL step_id — they are not renumbered — so every action SCTVA reports still traces back to the plan that was reviewed.

summary.description: Recomputed against the approved steps only. Leaving the original total_steps on a reduced step list produces a report that contradicts itself, which is exactly the kind of stale figure that hides a filtering bug.

approval.description: The audit record of the decision. This is what lets the audit trail and the feedback dataset agree with the plan that was actually executed.

source_plan_id.description: The plan_id this was reduced from. Preserved across a second reduction pass.

rejected_step_ids.description: Accumulated across reduction passes. Reducing an already-reduced plan must not erase what was rejected the first time: the second pass only sees the survivors, so its own rejected list would come back empty and the audit would lose the verdict.

pending_step_ids.description: Steps the developer neither approved nor rejected. These are NOT executed — only approved steps are.

original_total_steps.description: How many steps the RDP agent produced before approval, so the reduction is visible in the record.
